title: My God, I Thank Thee! May No Thought
description: My God, I Thank Thee! May No Thought in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Andrews Norton wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 327, “My God, I Thank Thee!”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: My God, I thank Thee! may no thought E'er deem Thy chas-tise-ments se-vere; But may this heart, by sor-row taught, Calm each wild wish, each id-le fear.

lines: My God, I thank Thee! may no thought
But may this heart, by sorrow taught,
Calm each wild wish, each idle fear.
Thy mercy bids all nature bloom;
The sun shines bright, and man is gay;
Thine equal mercy spreads the gloom
That darkens o'er his little day.
Full many a throb of grief and pain
Thy frail and erring child must know;
But not one prayer is breathed in vain,
Nor does one tear unheeded flow.
And, 'mid the wreck of human joy,
Let kneeling faith adore Thy will.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Andrews Norton died in 1853.
credits: Words by Andrews Norton (1786–1853), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
